column2: One should practice this natural bliss well until, in an instant, the inward state of the Self comes about of itself for the seeker.
Then, freed from practice, the king of yogis becomes perfected; that own form becomes the object of mind and speech for him.
When samadhi is being practiced, obstacles arise by force: lack of pursuit, laziness, craving for pleasure,
torpor, darkness, distraction, brilliance, sweat, and emptiness; such a multitude of obstacles is to be abandoned by the skilled in Brahman.
By the modification of being, there is being; by the modification of void, there is void; by the modification of Brahman, there is fullness; practice fullness by that.
Those who, leaving this purifying supreme modification called Brahman, live in vain are men equal to beasts.
Those who know the modification and, knowing, increase it — they are good people, blessed, to be revered in the three worlds.
Those whose modification is even, grown and fully ripe — they attain Brahman-hood; not the others, the talkers of words.
Skilled in talk of Brahman, but without the modification, passionate — they too, through ignorance, surely come and go again.
They do not stay even half a moment without the Brahman-made modification, as Brahma and others, Sanaka and others, Shuka and others stay.
The effect of which is the cause, its cause is born; the cause perishes in truth when, on reflection, the effect is absent.
Then the pure thing that is beyond the reach of speech arises; for those of pure mind, knowledge of the modification then is beyond.
The thing contemplated with intense force as certain: having brought the seen to non-seen, one should contemplate it in the form of Brahman.
The wise one should ever remain in bliss with a mind full of the savor of consciousness.

Then Kumara asked Shiva: "Tell me the nature of the undivided, one-savored, mere consciousness." The Supreme Shiva said: The seen is of undivided one savor; the world is of undivided one savor; being is of undivided one savor; one's own self is of undivided one savor.
The mantra is of undivided one savor; action is of undivided one savor; knowledge is of undivided one savor; water is of undivided one savor.
Earth is of undivided one savor; space is of undivided one savor; scripture is of undivided one savor; the three Vedas are of undivided one savor.
Brahman is of undivided one savor; the vow is of undivided one savor; the individual is of undivided one savor; the unborn is of undivided one savor.
Brahma is of undivided one savor; Hari is of undivided one savor; Rudra is of undivided one savor; I am of undivided one savor.
The Self is of undivided one savor; the teacher is of undivided one savor; the aim is of undivided one savor; splendor is of undivided one savor.
The body is of undivided one savor; the mind is of undivided one savor; the thought is of undivided one savor; happiness is of undivided one savor.
Knowledge is of undivided one savor; the imperishable is of undivided one savor; the eternal is of undivided one savor; the supreme is of undivided one savor.
Something is of undivided one savor; the highest is of undivided one savor; there is nothing other than the undivided one savor, nothing, O six-faced one.
Nothing is apart from the undivided one savor; indeed nothing; nothing at all apart from the undivided one savor; I am from the undivided one savor.
The gross is of undivided one savor; the subtle is of undivided form; the knowable is of undivided one savor; you are of undivided one savor.
The secret is of undivided one savor; the origin is of undivided one savor; the knower is of undivided one savor; the state is of undivided one savor.
The mother is of undivided one savor; the father is of undivided one savor; the brother is of undivided one savor; the husband is of undivided one savor.
The thread is of undivided one savor; Viraj is of undivided one savor; the limb is of undivided one savor; the head is of undivided one savor.
The inner is of undivided one savor; the outer is of undivided one savor; the full is of undivided one savor; the nectar is of undivided one savor.
Lineage is of undivided one savor; home is of undivided one savor; the secret is of undivided one savor; the moon is of undivided one savor.
The stars are of undivided one savor; the sun is of undivided one savor; the field is of undivided one savor; forbearance is of undivided one savor.
The peaceful is of undivided one savor; the quality-less is of undivided one savor; the witness is of undivided one savor; the friend is of undivided one savor.
The kinsman is of undivided one savor; the comrade is of undivided one savor; the king is of undivided one savor; the city is of undivided one savor.
The kingdom is of undivided one savor; the subjects are of undivided one savor; the sacred syllable is of undivided one savor; repetition is of undivided one savor.
Meditation is of undivided one savor; the state is of undivided one savor; the graspable is of undivided one savor; the great is of undivided one savor.
Light is of undivided one savor; wealth is of undivided one savor; food is of undivided one savor; the oblation is of undivided one savor.
The sacrifice is of undivided one savor; repetition is of undivided one savor; heaven is of undivided one savor; oneself is of undivided one savor.
One should contemplate all as undivided one savor, mere consciousness; mere consciousness, mere consciousness, the undivided one savor, the supreme.
Mere consciousness free of becoming — all is only mere consciousness; and all this is made of mere consciousness, made of consciousness alone.
They know the state of Self as mere consciousness, undivided one savor; all worlds are mere consciousness; the speaker and the delighted are made of consciousness.
Space, earth, water, wind, fire, Brahma, Hari, Shiva — whatever is and whatever is not, all is only mere consciousness.
Everything undivided one savor, whatever is only mere consciousness; the past, the present and the future — all is only mere consciousness.
Substance and time are mere consciousness; knowledge and the knowable are consciousness alone; the knower is of the form of mere consciousness; all is made of consciousness.
Conversation is mere consciousness; whatever is, is only mere consciousness; the unreal and the real are mere consciousness; the beginning and end are ever made of consciousness.
Beginning and end are mere consciousness; teacher and disciple are made of consciousness; seer and seen, if they exist, are mere consciousness, ever made of consciousness.
All wonder is mere consciousness; the body is only mere consciousness; the subtle body and the cause exist not apart from mere consciousness.
I and you are mere consciousness; the formed and formless are made of consciousness; merit and sin are mere consciousness; the individual is a body of mere consciousness.
From mere consciousness there is no intention; from mere consciousness there is no feeling; from mere consciousness there is no mantra; from mere consciousness there is no deity.

From mere consciousness there are no guardians of the quarters; from mere consciousness there is no worldly activity; Brahman is beyond mere consciousness; from mere consciousness there is none at all.
From mere consciousness there is no illusion; from mere consciousness there is no worship; from mere consciousness there is nothing to be thought; from mere consciousness there is no truth.
From mere consciousness there are no sheaths and the like; from mere consciousness there is no wealth; from mere consciousness there is no silence; from mere consciousness there is no non-silence.
From mere consciousness there is no dispassion; all is only mere consciousness; whatever and however much is mere consciousness, whatever and however much is seen,
whatever and however much is far away, all is only mere consciousness; whatever and however much are the elements and so on, whatever and however much is perceived,
whatever and however much are the Vedantas, all is only mere consciousness; from mere consciousness there is no going; from mere consciousness there is no liberation;
from mere consciousness there is no aim; all is only mere consciousness; Brahman of undivided one savor does not exist apart from mere consciousness.
In scripture, in me, in you, and in the Lord you are of undivided one savor; whoever knows in this one-form manner, "I am that" —
by a single knowledge there would be liberation; in right knowledge one becomes the teacher oneself.

Kumara asked his father: "Tell me the experience of the Self." The Supreme Shiva said: I am of the nature of supreme Brahman, I am supreme bliss. I am of the form of knowledge alone; I am the supreme alone.
I am of peaceful form alone; I am made of consciousness alone; I am of eternal form alone; I am everlasting alone.
I am of the form of sattva alone; abandoning "I," I am; I am of the nature of being devoid of all; I am made of the space of consciousness.
I am of the form of the Fourth alone; I am alone beyond the Fourth; I am ever of the form of consciousness; I am made of consciousness-bliss.
I am of the form of the alone; I am ever of pure form; I am of the form of knowledge alone; I am the beloved alone.
I am of the nature of non-conception; I am desireless, free of disease; I am ever of unattached nature; I am changeless and undying.
I am ever of one-savor form; I am ever a body of mere consciousness; I am of unlimited form; I have the form of undivided bliss.
I am of the form of being and supreme bliss; I am consciousness and supreme bliss; I am of the form of the inmost; I am beyond speech and mind.
I am of the nature of Self-bliss; I am ever true bliss; I am of the nature of delighting in the Self; this Self is ever Sadashiva.
I am of the form of self-luminosity; I am the savor of the light of the Self; I am without beginning, middle or end; I am like space.
I am the mere being of eternal pure consciousness-bliss, imperishable; I am the one eternal, awake, purely being-consciousness-bliss.
I am of the nature of the eternal remainder; I am ever beyond all; I am of the nature beyond form; I am a body of supreme space.
I am of the nature of the bliss of the fullness; I am ever without speech; I am of the form of the support of all; I am ever a mass of consciousness.
I am devoid of body-notion; I am ever devoid of anxiety; I am devoid of mind's modifications; I am of one savor, the Self of consciousness.
I am devoid of all that is seen; I am indeed of the form of the seer; I am ever of full form; I am ever satisfied.
I am Brahman; all would be I; I am consciousness itself; I alone, I alone am, of the nature of the fullness of space.
I alone am the great Self; I alone am higher than the highest; I appear as another; I alone am like the body.
I appear like a disciple; this is the support of the three worlds; I am beyond the three times; I am worshipped by the Vedas.
I am determined by scripture; I am established in the mind; nothing is apart from me; nothing is abandoned by me, nor the earth.
Whatever is other than me — be certain it does not exist; I am Brahman, I am perfected, I am ever eternally pure.
I am the attributeless, the Self alone; I am ever formless; I am Brahman alone; I am ageless, I am deathless.
By myself I shine by myself; by myself I am ever being; by myself I rest in the Self; by myself the supreme goal.
By myself I break by myself; by myself I delight by myself; by myself I am light by myself; by myself I am splendor by myself.
In my own Self I shall delight by myself; in my own Self alone I shall look; seated happy in my own Self, with only my Self remaining.
In my own consciousness I shall stay by myself; in the kingdom of my own Self I shall delight in bliss; seated on the throne of my own Self, I shall think of nothing else than the Self.
Mere form of consciousness is Brahman, being-consciousness-bliss, non-dual; I am a mass of bliss; I am Brahman alone.
I am ever void of all; I am blissful as the Self of all; I am of the nature of eternal bliss; I am ever the space of the Self.
I alone am the space of the heart, of the nature of the sun of consciousness; by the Self I am satisfied in the Self; I am formless and imperishable.
I am devoid of the number one; I am of the nature of eternally liberated; I am subtler than space; I am devoid of beginning and end.
I am of the form of the light of all; I am the bliss of the high and low; I am of the nature of mere being; I am of the nature of pure liberation.
I am of the nature of true bliss; I am a mass of knowledge-bliss; I am of the form of mere knowledge; I am marked by being-consciousness-bliss.
All this is only Brahman; nothing is other than Brahman; that alone I am, ever bliss; I am Brahman, the eternal.
You, "that" — nothing is other than me; I am of the nature of consciousness; I alone am Shiva, the supreme.
I am of the nature of beyond-being; I alone am of the nature of happiness; devoid of a thing to be witnessed, I have no witness-hood ever.
Being Brahman alone, I am the eternal Self; I alone am the primal remainder; I alone am the remainder.
I am freed from name and form; I am a body of bliss; I am of the form of absence of senses; I am of the nature of all existence.
I am devoid of bondage and liberation; I am a body of eternal bliss; I am mere primal consciousness; I am of undivided one savor.
I am beyond speech and mind; I am blissful everywhere; I am of full form everywhere; I am made of the bliss of the fullness.
I am of the form of satisfaction everywhere; I am the savor of supreme nectar; the one without a second, being, Brahman alone am I; no doubt.
I am of the nature of the void of all; I am the object of all scriptures; I am free, I am of the form of liberation, I have the form of the bliss of nirvana.
I am mere true knowledge; I am blissful with mere being; I am of a form beyond the Fourth; I am of the nature of non-conception.
I am ever of unborn form; I am passionless, stainless; I am pure, I am awake, I am eternal, I am the lord.
I am of the nature of the meaning of Om; I am made of the stainless; I am of the nature of the form of consciousness; I am not "I," nor am I "he."
